newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs down, but recover from fall on machinery data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs down, but recover from fall on machinery data.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures closed off a little, but the market was firmly underpinned by strong buying on dips on Tuesday.

An upbeat tone in the Tokyo bourse and the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) tight money market operation for the first time in about a year, save the last day of a banking reserve reporting period pushed the contract down in the morning.

In the afternoon, stronger-than-expected July machinery orders data made a dent for the market. But soon the December erased much of losses. It ended at 121.27, down 0.07 from Monday. Volume was 55,185 contracts.
Strong buying on dips countered these negative factors, dealers said.
The Economic Planning Agency (EPA) announced that machinery orders grew 13.6 percent in July from the previous month, well above market expectations.
The release of the machinery orders data was followed by a large-lot sale, but the market not only digested the sale but recouped much of its losses later.
A securities firm dealer said some investors were buying cash bonds. But many said they could not pinpoint exactly who was the main driving force of the buyers of the December.
In the cash bond market, the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGBs were yielding 2.940 percent, up 0.010 from Monday.
